title: Locally condensed finite-strain plane-stress Neo-Hookean membrane
summary: Enforces P33=0 through a positive local thickness stretch and uses the same condensed energy, in-plane first-Piola stress, and Schur-complement tangent in static and Explicit finite-strain workflows.

science.statement: A thin two-dimensional hyperelastic membrane is reduced from the three-dimensional compressible Neo-Hookean energy by solving a positive out-of-plane stretch at each material point such that P33 vanishes.

equations.label: local plane-stress condition
equations.description: The thickness stretch is an eliminated local variable, not a prescribed Poisson estimate.

equations.label: condensed membrane tangent
equations.description: The same local condition is differentiated for small-on-large acoustic analysis.

inputs.name: in-plane deformation gradient and material
inputs.description: The material supplies E, nu, and optional reference density.

outputs.name: thickness stretch, condensed energy, P, and tangent
outputs.type: local scalar, scalar density, in-plane tensor, and fourth-order tensor
outputs.description: All outputs satisfy the same local P33=0 reduction.

assumptions: A homogeneous through-thickness membrane response with no transverse shear is appropriate.
The three-dimensional parent material is compressible Neo-Hookean with finite bulk modulus.
conventions: The two-dimensional Study must declare assumption='plane_stress'.
J means the complete three-dimensional determinant including the condensed thickness stretch.
Incremental wave speeds use the reference density and a declared reference/current propagation direction.
applicability: Thin hyperelastic sheets, plane-stress parameter studies, and the experimental weak-interface dynamic-fracture route.
limitations: Local plane-stress condensation does not by itself prove freedom from in-plane volumetric locking on arbitrary meshes.
A thin-three-dimensional comparison, general mixed or F-bar Explicit route, and prestrained surface-wave secular solution remain open validation gates.

usage.minimal_example:
study = studies.dynamic_solid(dimension=2, assumption='plane_stress', method='explicit')
material = model.material(constitutive.neo_hookean_plane_stress(young=1000, poisson=0.49, density=1))
step = model.step(target=u, material=material, steps=100)

validation_rules: Require positive thickness stretch and P33 closure.
Compare the Schur-complement tangent with finite differences of the condensed first-Piola response.
Reject a plane-strain material under a plane-stress Study and vice versa.
Keep general near-incompressible locking claims outside this material's evidence scope.

references.title: Wang, Fineberg, and Needleman (2025), transition from crack-type to supershear-type to spall-type dynamics
